logo.redo: THE OPERATOR'S INSTRUCTION FOR VINCENT, 4 Nov 2026: 'He sent a logo already and Vince may need to redo it within the exact same style but to make it suitable for the site as I think it's a low-res image.' The files are JPEGs (1600 x 535, 65 KB; 2048 x 684, 64 KB), compressed, on solid black, with no transparent or vector version. If they are not sharp enough where the site uses them, recreate the logo in exactly the same style, not a new design: 'TRUELINE' in the same classical serif capitals with the taller T, the same bevelled metallic-blue gradient with its chrome highlight, 'FINISHES' beneath in the same spaced serif capitals between the two thin tapering blue lines, on black; as an SVG or a large transparent PNG, at a resolution suitable for the site. Ask Brandon for the original file first: if he has it, nothing needs redrawing.

facts.fact: Baildon’s conservation areas contain a mixture of 17th-, 18th-, 19th- and early-20th-century buildings, including workers’ cottages, substantial houses, churches, shops, offices, mills and industrial premises; decorators working there need to distinguish heritage-sensitive repairs from ordinary repainting.
facts.label: PROPERTY TYPES

facts.fact: Hallcliffe and Northgate contain large areas of 19th-century terraced housing, making exterior masonry preparation, windows and doors, stair halls, kitchens and compact-room redecorations particularly relevant trade work.
facts.label: PROPERTY TYPES

facts.fact: Baildon is surrounded on three sides by open countryside and is bounded by the River Aire and Leeds and Liverpool Canal, so exterior painting businesses should expect varied exposure, damp-risk considerations and access requirements across urban and edge-of-town properties.
facts.label: LANDMARKS

facts.fact: The area between the A6038 and River Aire is predominantly commercial and industrial, alongside housing, creating a local market for commercial painting and decorating as well as residential work.
facts.label: LANDMARKS

facts.fact: Baildon has experienced extensive housing development over the past century, while new development is now constrained by limited suitable sites; this supports a mixed workload of refurbishment, kitchen renovation, wallpapering and redecoration in existing homes rather than relying only on new-build projects.
facts.label: PROPERTY TYPES

labels.PROPERTY TYPES: Stone cottages and farmhouses dating from the 17th and 18th centuries; substantial late-18th- and early-19th-century houses; 19th-century stone workers’ terraces around Hallcliffe and Northgate; former mill and industrial buildings; early-20th-century houses; and extensive later-20th-century suburban developments, including newer housing around High Fold. These materials and eras create regular demand for breathable masonry-compatible coatings, timber repairs, interior redecoration, wallpapering, and careful work around retained period features.
labels.NEIGHBOURHOODS: Baildon Village Centre, Baildon Green, Baildon Station Road, Hallcliffe, Northgate, High Fold, Charlestown, Tong Park
labels.LANDMARKS: Baildon Moor, Baildon Bank, Roberts Park, River Aire, Leeds and Liverpool Canal, Shipley Glen, Bracken Hall Countryside Centre, Baildon Hall, Baildon Green Quarries
labels.LOCAL CHARACTER: Baildon is a substantial Aire Valley town rather than a small village, with a locally recognised “village centre” surrounded by many neighbourhoods, strong commuter links, and an attractive setting between the River Aire and moorland. Locals and planning documents associate its identity with “Baildon Village Centre,” Baildon Green’s tightly packed stone buildings, dramatic views, and the town’s rural and walking connections towards Baildon Moor and Shipley Glen.

hubs.contentNote: THE HEADLINE HUB: the whole trade, Brandon's 'all aspects of painting and decorating' (WhatsApp 27 Oct 2026). Articles are titled 'Painting and Decorating in [Town]' and answer the main search in every town, 'painter and decorator [town]'. Cover everything TrueLine Finishes does, briefly, and link to the hub that goes deeper: interior painting (walls, ceilings, every room, all the woodwork), exterior painting (masonry, woodwork, windows, doors, fascias and soffits), wallpapering and commercial work, with the careful preparation that goes into all of it. From individual rooms to full property redecorations, for homes and businesses (Brandon's own advert); say in passing that the work is for both. Sell quality, not price: attention to detail, lasting finishes and treating the property with care are Brandon's own words; never 'cheap', never a price. Over eight years' experience (the operator's wording of Brandon's 'eight') is the only figure.
